## Purpose and entry points
CPython 3.16 alpha is the reference Python implementation: a C runtime and interpreter, bundled standard library, extension-module platform, developer tools, and platform packaging. Primary executable entry points are `Programs/python.c` and `Modules/main.c`; initialization, configuration, and shutdown are owned by `Python/pylifecycle.c` and `Python/initconfig.c`.

## Language front end and compilation
Source text flows from tokenizer/lexer through the PEG parser into AST and compiler stages. The grammar is the authoritative language definition in `Grammar/python.gram`; parser implementation and public PEG API are in `Parser/parser.c` and `Parser/peg_api.c`. AST creation/processing and compilation then produce executable code objects/bytecode via `Python/ast.c`, `Python/compile.c`, and `Python/codegen.c`. Generated parser and opcode artifacts are a key boundary: grammar or instruction-definition changes require generators under `Tools/peg_generator` and `Tools/cases_generator`.

## Execution engine and runtime state
The interpreter evaluates compiled code, manages frames, exceptions, tracing, specialization/optimization, and optional JIT infrastructure. Main evaluation logic is in `Python/ceval.c`; frame and thread/interpreter state are represented through `Python/frame.c` and `Python/pystate.c`. Adaptive optimization and tiered execution are concentrated in `Python/specialize.c`, `Python/optimizer.c`, and generated instruction cases such as `Python/generated_cases.c.h`. JIT support spans `Python/jit.c`, publishing/unwinding code, and build-time tooling in `Tools/jit/build.py`.

## Object model, memory, and public C boundary
`Objects/` implements Python’s fundamental data model: object/type behavior, containers, numeric/string types, weak references, and garbage-sensitive semantics. Central implementations include `Objects/object.c`, `Objects/typeobject.c`, and `Objects/dictobject.c`. Allocation combines CPython allocators with vendored mimalloc sources under `Objects/mimalloc`. Public extension ABI/API contracts are exposed from `Include/Python.h` and object-specific headers; internal runtime-only contracts live under `Include/internal`, which should not be treated as stable extension interfaces.

## Imports, builtins, native modules, and standard library
Runtime startup installs builtins and import machinery, then loads Python modules from `Lib/` and native built-in/extension modules from `Modules/`. Import implementation is centered in `Python/import.c` and Python bootstrap logic in `Lib/importlib/_bootstrap.py`. Core native modules include I/O (`Modules/_io/_iomodule.c`), SSL (`Modules/_ssl.c`), and SQLite (`Modules/_sqlite/module.c`), bridging to platform or third-party libraries. `Lib/` supplies the standard-library Python layer, including asynchronous runtime APIs in `Lib/asyncio` and process/concurrency abstractions in `Lib/multiprocessing`.

## Build, platforms, and delivery
Unix-like builds are configured by `configure`/`configure.ac` and built through `Makefile.pre.in`; generated sources and frozen modules are orchestrated by tools such as `Tools/build/freeze_modules.py`. Windows uses Visual Studio projects rooted at `PCbuild/pcbuild.sln`, while `PC/layout/main.py` assembles distributable Windows layouts. Dedicated platform paths support Android, Apple mobile targets, WASI, and Emscripten: `Platforms/Android`, `Platforms/Apple`, `Platforms/WASI/_build.py`, and `Platforms/emscripten`. External dependencies are platform/configuration dependent and materially include OpenSSL, SQLite, libffi, Tcl/Tk, compression libraries, and system toolchains.

## Validation and operational infrastructure
The regression-test runner is `Lib/test/libregrtest/main.py`; it executes broad runtime, library, embedding, ABI, and platform tests. CI runs in GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines, with cross-platform workflows under `.github/workflows` and Azure definitions under `.azure-pipelines`. Documentation is a separately built Sphinx-style deliverable rooted at `Doc/conf.py`, with API documentation providing an important compatibility boundary for `Include/` and `Modules/` changes.
